text.p: The Italian debt market closed just off session highs after the September Btp Liffe contract hit a new historic high of 135.20, although traders said shorter term paper on the cash market were showing signs of fatigue.

"The upward trend has been set by Bunds," one operator said. "The Btp continues to be supported by convergence hopes and a raft of Eurolire issues on Wednesday has also helped bullish sentiment," he added.
The spread over the benchmark 10-year Bund narrowed to a new low of 106 basis points during the session.

Dealers were now looking for the spread to narrow to 100 bps. "The bet is that Italy will join the single European currency and the market is anticipating the event, tightening the spreads," one said.
"The trend of Btps over the coming days will still depend a lot on Bunds because there will still be more punting on the spreads than on the contract itself," another added.

In cash bonds, the February 2007 Bbt gained 60 bps to 100.92 yielding 6.71 percent. The March 2002 was up 20 bps to 100.73 yielding 6.15 percent while the February 15, 2000 bond was offering 5.96 percent at 100.24.
